sites.why: Rule 8: OpenAI chat.completions ('gpt' branch of get_batch_responses_from_llm, review ensemble) on openai.OpenAI() default endpoint with OPENAI_API_KEY; model is a runtime parameter and the repo's OpenAI literals include catalog ids (gpt-4o, gpt-4o-mini, gpt-4.1...). Caveat: the only production caller (launch_scientist.py:270/296 -> perform_review) passes the literal 'gpt-4o-2024-05-13', which is not in the catalog or dated equivalences; also uses n=5.
Rule 2: llama branch of get_batch_responses_from_llm; client is the OpenRouter client (base_url https://openrouter.ai/api/v1, OPENROUTER_API_KEY) and the model is an OpenRouter id.

Rule 6: Anthropic messages.create ('claude' branch); client from create_client is anthropic.Anthropic() (default endpoint, ANTHROPIC_API_KEY) for claude-* models (AnthropicBedrock/AnthropicVertex clients for bedrock/ and vertex_ai/ ids reach the same call). Model is runtime and none of the repo's Claude literals (claude-3-5-sonnet-20240620, claude-3-5-sonnet-20241022, bedrock/vertex variants) are Router catalog ids.
sites.adjudication: Rule 6. For claude-* ids, create_client returns anthropic.Anthropic() (llm.py:320): the default endpoint with ANTHROPIC_API_KEY from env, so rules 2 and 4 do not apply to the shipped default. The model is chosen at runtime (args.model, choices=AVAILABLE_LLMS; default claude-3-5-sonnet-20240620 at launch_scientist.py:51). None of the repo's Claude literals are catalog ids or dated equivalents: claude-3-5-sonnet-20240620/20241022 at llm.py:15-16, plus the bedrock/ and vertex_ai/ variants at llm.py

sites.why: Rule 8: OpenAI chat.completions ('gpt' branch of get_response_from_llm) on openai.OpenAI() default endpoint with OPENAI_API_KEY; model is runtime (--model / client_model, plus review literal gpt-4o-2024-05-13 for reflections/meta-review) and the repo's OpenAI literals include catalog ids.

Rule 8: OpenAI chat.completions ('o1'/'o3' branch) on openai.OpenAI() default endpoint with OPENAI_API_KEY; model is runtime and repo literals include catalog ids o1 / o3-mini (o1-mini, o1-preview are not).
Rule 2: llama branch of get_response_from_llm; create_client('llama3.1-405b') returns openai.OpenAI(base_url='https://openrouter.ai/api/v1', OPENROUTER_API_KEY).
Rule 2: deepseek-chat/deepseek-coder branch; create_client returns openai.OpenAI(base_url='https://api.deepseek.com', DEEPSEEK_API_KEY).
sites.adjudication: Rule 2. This branch only runs for model in ['deepseek-chat','deepseek-coder'] (llm.py:232). Every production caller pairs the client with the model through create_client(args.model) (launch_scientist.py:339, generate_ideas.py:528, perform_writeup.py:539), and for these ids create_client returns openai.OpenAI(api_key=DEEPSEEK_API_KEY, base_url='https://api.deepseek.com') (llm.py:332-337), which is another vendor's host.

sites.why: Rule 2: deepseek-reasoner branch; client is openai.OpenAI(base_url='https://api.deepseek.com', DEEPSEEK_API_KEY).
sites.adjudication: Rule 2. The deepseek-reasoner branch (llm.py:247) is only reached with the client that create_client builds for that id: openai.OpenAI(base_url='https://api.deepseek.com', DEEPSEEK_API_KEY) (llm.py:332-337). That is another vendor's endpoint.

sites.why: Rule 2: gemini branch; create_client returns openai.OpenAI(base_url='https://generativelanguage.googleapis.com/v1beta/openai/', GEMINI_API_KEY), i.e. Google's OpenAI-compatible endpoint.
sites.adjudication: Rule 2. The gemini branch (llm.py:260) gets openai.OpenAI(api_key=GEMINI_API_KEY, base_url='https://generativelanguage.googleapis.com/v1beta/openai/') from create_client (llm.py:344-349). That is Google's OpenAI-compatible host, a non-OpenAI base_url. Rule 2 comes before rule 7, so this is kept, not handoff.
